about.title: About IF Builder
about.subtitle: Learn the mission and values behind IF Builder.

project.p1: IF Builder is an editor I developed to create interactive fiction - textual narratives where the player decides what happens next.
project.p2: Here, interactive fictions are written in scenes. It's easy to visualize where each choice takes the player and how paths cross. If you want something to happen only if the player has a specific item or made a previous choice, the editor easily handles that.
project.p3: When finished, the editor exports a .zip file that works in any browser. Your story leaves the editor and goes straight to whoever wants to play. And if that person uses IF Builder, they can import the .zip file into the editor and see how you created your story. Maybe even make a remix?

support.title: Why support?
support.p1: IF Builder is a free, non-profit project, and its operation is funded by the developer.
support.p2: If this tool is useful for you, consider making a donation of any amount. All funds raised go exclusively to paying the site's infrastructure costs, including maintenance and future improvements.
support.p3: If you have suggestions, feedback, or want to share your stories, send an email to:

guide.title: Quick Guide
guide.intro: IF Builder allows you to create interactive fictions, text-based narratives where the player interacts with the story through choices or verbs. The fiction is composed of Scenes, where the user reads descriptions, observes images, and makes decisions to interact with objects and navigate the world.

scenes.title: 1. Scene Editor
scenes.desc: Each scene is a location or moment in your game.
scenes.item1: Name and Description: Set the title and text the player will see when entering the scene.
scenes.item2: Interactive Text: Use < > around a word to make it clickable (e.g. <door>).
scenes.item3: Image and Music: Each scene can have its own background image and soundtrack.
scenes.item4: Home Scene: Define which scene will be the starting point in the sidebar.
scenes.item5: Ending Scene: Mark a scene as final to end the narrative.

objects.title: 2. Object Library
objects.desc: Objects are global and can be reused across multiple scenes.
objects.item2: Examine: Detailed description the player sees when using "examine" or "look".
objects.item3: Image: Add an optional image to represent the object.
objects.item4: Collectible: Mark if the object can be added to the inventory.

interactions.title: 3. Interactions (The heart of the game)
interactions.desc: Defines what happens when the player types a verb.
interactions.item1: Verbs: Words that trigger the action (e.g. open, use, take).
interactions.item4: Result: Go to scene, change text, or play vignette.
interactions.tip: The system understands various orders (e.g. "Use key on door").

globals.title: 4. Global Verbs
globals.desc: Verbs that work in any scene of the game.
globals.item2: Description: Standard response for each global verb.

vignettes.title: 5. Vignettes
vignettes.desc: Cinematic screens that enrich the narrative.
vignettes.item1: Opening: Displayed before the game starts (title screen).
vignettes.item2: Transition: Played during interactions for dramatic moments.
vignettes.item3: Conclusion: Shown at the end of the game (victory/defeat).
vignettes.tip: Customize image, music, text alignment, and animations.

trackers.title: 6. Consequence Trackers
trackers.item1: Initial and Max Value: Defines the scale (e.g. 0/100).
trackers.item2: Consequence Scene: Where the player goes when reaching the limit.
trackers.item3: Customization: Choose color, icon, and bar mode (normal or inverted).

map.title: 7. Connections Map
map.desc: Visualize the structure of your game graphically.
map.item1: Bird's Eye View: See all scenes and how they connect.
map.item2: Quick Navigation: Click on a scene on the map to edit it.
map.item3: Positioning: Drag scenes to organize the visual layout.

preview.title: 9. Preview and Test
preview.item1: Use the Preview button to test the whole experience.
preview.item2: Test from any scene you are editing.
preview.item3: Check if verbs and interactions work as expected.

export.title: 10. Saving and Loading Projects
export.warning: IMPORTANT: Remember to ALWAYS save your project, as the editor does not record any sessions. If you leave without saving, just like in older programs, you will lose ALL your progress!
export.desc: When your game is ready (or to save your progress):
export.item1: Fully test all scenes and endings using the Preview Mode.
export.item2: Click the Save button (floppy disk icon) in the top menu.
export.item3: Give your project a name. The editor will download a unified .zip file.
export.item5: To continue editing: Use the Load button uploading this same .zip file.

manualModal.title: User Manual
manualModal.subtitle: Learn how to create your interactive adventure
manualModal.intro: The IF Builder allows you to create Interactive Fiction games. The game is composed of Scenes, where the player reads descriptions, looks at images, and types verbs to interact with Objects and navigate the world.
manualModal.section1Intro: Each scene is a location or moment in your game. Configure:
manualModal.section1Item1: Interactive Text: Use the <word> syntax in the description. This will make the word clickable in the game.
manualModal.section1Item2: Image and Music: Each scene can have a unique background image and soundtrack.
manualModal.section1Item3: Start Scene: Set which scene will be the starting point.
manualModal.section2Intro: Objects are items that can be in a scene. They are global: you create an object once and can link it to multiple scenes.
manualModal.section2Item1: Examine: Define a detailed description that the player will see.
manualModal.section3Intro: Interactions define what happens when the player types a verb.
manualModal.verbsDesc: List of words that trigger the action (e.g., open, unlock, use).
manualModal.targetDesc: The object in the scene the player wants to interact with (e.g., Door).
manualModal.reqDesc: The item the player MUST have in their inventory (e.g., Key).
manualModal.resDesc: What happens after the verb (e.g., go to another scene).
manualModal.tip: 💡 Tip: The player can type in any order. The system will automatically identify the keywords.
manualModal.section4Intro: Use trackers to create complex systems like Health, Money, or Stress.
manualModal.section4Item1: Interactions can increase or decrease a tracker's value.
manualModal.section4Item2: When a tracker reaches its maximum value, the player is automatically transported to a Consequence Scene.
manualModal.section5Item1: Use the Preview button to test the entire experience.
manualModal.section5Item2: Click Export Game to download a .zip file.
manualModal.section5Item3: Extract the zip and open the index.html file in any browser to play or share!
